newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-MEXICO SURVIVE COLOMBIA FIGHTBACK TO WIN 2-1.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEXICO SURVIVE COLOMBIA FIGHTBACK TO WIN 2-1.

text.p: Mexico became the first team to score more than one goal in a game in the Copa America when they beat Colombia 2-1 in the opening group C match on Friday.
Striker Luis Hernandez struck twice in the first fifteen minutes but Mexico were lucky to hold out for a win.
Hamilton Ricard pulled a goal back on the hour for Colombia, who dominated the second half but wasted several good chances to equalise.
Three of the previous four games in the tournament, which began Wednesday, had ended 1-0 and the fourth was scoreless.
Both teams are involved in World Cup qualifying matches and have rested their star players for the Copa.
Colombia's newcomers showed the same faults as their more seasoned colleagues with their neat approach work wasted by poor finishing.

Hernandez struck the first blow after 10 minutes when he scored with a long range shot. He stunned the Colombians again five minutes later when he rose above two defenders and headed the ball in following a cross from the left.

The Mexican team, however, produced no other real attacks in the entire game apart from the ones they scored from and Hernandez spent the rest of the match getting into kicking and punching matches with opposing defenders.

Ricard reduced the deficit when he beat the Mexican defence to a corner and scored. Ricard, standing in for the absent Faustino Asprilla, missed good chances on either side of his goal as Colombia dominated the second half.
